2026-08-31.content:
You can use [access control list (ACL) policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/use-acl-policies) to secure access to your clusters. You can enable fine-grained
security by restricting user and service access to specific keys, commands,
operations, and Pub/Sub channels. This feature is [Generally Available](https://docs.cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages).

summary.title: Secure your Memorystore clusters with ACL policies
summary.summary: Enhance your Memorystore cluster security with access control list (ACL) policies. This feature, now Generally Available, allows for fine-grained control over user and service access to specific keys, commands, and operations, ensuring robust data protection.

2026-08-10.content: You can use the Google Cloud console to secure access to your clusters by using [basic token-based authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/manage-basic-auth). This feature is available in [Preview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages).

summary.title: Secure cluster access with basic authentication
summary.summary: You can now secure access to your clusters using basic token-based authentication. This new feature, available in Preview, can be managed through the Google Cloud console.

2025-09-30.content: The [customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/about-cmek) feature for Memorystore for Redis Cluster is now [Generally Available](https://cloud.google.com/products#product-launch-stages).

summary.title: Memorystore for Redis Cluster Now Supports CMEK
summary.summary: We are pleased to announce that Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for Memorystore for Redis Cluster is now Generally Available. This feature allows you to manage your own encryption keys for enhanced security.
